issues.title: Generic Lyapunov error certification
issues.failure_explanation: For a general Hurwitz matrix, the Lyapunov operator is invertible, but its smallest singular value need not equal twice the smallest singular value of the matrix. For example, take A=[[-1,10],[0,-1]], set the Lyapunov forcing to zero, and let the exact solution be X=0 and the admissible positive-definite approximation be X_l=E=[[50,5],[5,1]]. Then R=AE+EA^T=diag(0,-2), so ||E||_2 is approximately 50.505, whereas the old right-hand side is approximately 10.10. The preceding inverse-operator calculation proves only the bound with denominator sigma_min(L).
issues.overall_effect: The residual terms in teo1 are not certified for general nonnormal Hurwitz matrices. The same false denominator also propagates to eq33, the scaling in eq:52, the fixed and dynamic Lyapunov stopping thresholds, and the generic linear-cost discussion. Proposition prop2 itself remains valid under its stated contraction assumption.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let ℒ = I_n⊗A + A⊗I_n. Replace 2σ_min(A) by σ_min(ℒ) in prop1 and in every residual term of teo1, and propagate the same correction through eq33, the scaling in eq:52, and the fixed and dynamic Lyapunov stopping tolerances. For general Hurwitz A, retain certification only using a rigorously computed or lower-bounded σ_min(ℒ), and replace the generic linear-cost claim by the correct n²-dimensional-operator cost qualification; linear-cost certification may be claimed only for explicitly structured cases admitting a cheap valid coercivity bound.
issues.why_classification: The inverse-operator argument locally establishes the corrected residual bounds, so the formal certification can remain valid on the full Hurwitz class. On that same route, however, the generic linear-cost certification is lost: σ_min(ℒ) is not controlled by σ_min(A) for nonnormal Hurwitz matrices and generally requires work at the n²-dimensional operator scale. This withdraws a central affected complexity guarantee. Restricting the efficient result to dissipative or similarly structured matrices instead excludes a substantial advertised regime, and no source-supported route preserves both genericity and linear cost without essentially new machinery.

issues.title: Observability defect matrix
issues.failure_explanation: The balanced output matrix has size p by n, so the old term C_j C_j^T is p by p and generally cannot be added to the n by n Lyapunov terms. Moreover, Sigma_j A_j^T is not the dual term generated by differentiating X_o^T Sigma_j X_o and generally makes the alleged defect matrix nonsymmetric. The appendix instead uses A_j^T Sigma_j+Sigma_j A_j+C_j^T C_j, so its argument supports the corrected, not the stated, definition.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the observability defect eigenvalue and hence the observability part of the estimator in teo5 are generally undefined or unsupported. The iterated PBR bound in teo6 inherits this defect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the observability-defect definition in teo5 by M_o(j) = bar(A_j)^T Sigma_j + Sigma_j bar(A_j) + bar(C_j)^T bar(C_j), and let all later references to M_o use this corrected definition. No proof or estimator restructuring is needed for this issue.
issues.why_classification: The dimensions force bar(C_j)^T bar(C_j), while symmetry and differentiation of X_o^T Sigma_j X_o force Sigma_j bar(A_j). The appendix already uses exactly this uniquely determined expression. Thus the defect is a transcriptional transpose/orientation error, and the intended reader can correct it without repairing any inference; teo6 then inherits the same intended result.

issues.title: Observability contribution in the PBR estimator
issues.failure_explanation: Even after the observability matrix itself is correctly oriented, the old definition of H_o multiplies ||X_o||^2 by lambda_1(M_c). The observability differential inequality in the appendix produces lambda_1(M_o), while M_c occurs only with X_c. Thus the proof supports an H_o defined using M_o, and the old M_c term can undercount the required contribution because the paper establishes no comparison between these defect matrices.
issues.overall_effect: The output-error bound in teo5 can omit part of the observability contribution, and teo6 inherits that unsupported estimator through its iteration of teo5.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the definition of H_{o,q}, replace λ_1(M_c(q(t_k^+))) by λ_1(M_o(q(t_k^+))) on every switching interval, while leaving H_{c,q} weighted by M_c. Use this corrected H_{o,q} when teo5 is iterated in teo6.
issues.why_classification: The observability differential inequality and the appendix's final combined estimate already use M_o with X_o, whereas M_c is used only with X_c. These parts of the old source uniquely identify the lone c-subscript in H_{o,q} as a copied symbol. Correcting it requires no new inference or proof change and restores the source-forced intended estimator.

issues.title: Synthetic-example dissipativity

failure_location.quote: Moreover, both $\fA_1$ and $\fA_2$ are normal matrices, so the hypothesis of \Cref{teo4} holds.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that both displayed matrices are normal and that normality establishes the hypothesis of teo4. The old paper's matrix definitions instead show that, for n>1, A1 is a one-sided bidiagonal matrix and A2 has unequal upper and lower off-diagonal magnitudes, so their products with their transposes do not commute. What the matrices actually establish is strict dissipativity: A1+A1^T has diagonal -2 and off-diagonal 1/2, while A2+A2^T has diagonal -4 and off-diagonal 3/5, making both negative definite. Thus the theorem remains applicable, but the stated matrix property and justification are false.
issues.overall_effect: The example's invocation of teo4 has a valid dissipativity justification, but the old prose misstates that justification as normality. No formal theorem statement is invalidated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the normality claim by the statement that A_1 and A_2 are strictly dissipative. Supply the routine check that A_1+A_1^T has diagonal −2 and off-diagonal 1/2, while A_2+A_2^T has diagonal −4 and off-diagonal 3/5; strict diagonal dominance, or Gershgorin's theorem, makes both symmetric matrices negative definite. The invocation of teo4 then remains unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The matrices are genuinely nonnormal for n>1, so the old justification is mathematically false rather than a harmless transcription. Repair requires a short definiteness argument, but that argument is local and routine and preserves the example, teo4's hypotheses, and its applicability without any weakening or downstream change.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Moreover, both $\fA_1$ and $\fA_2$ are dissipative matrices, so the hypothesis of \Cref{teo4} holds.
